items.followUp: Define an orbital and state how it differs from a shell.

rubric.why: A shell is a principal energy level around the nucleus.
rubric.description: Defines a shell as a main energy level around the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a shell as a main energy level around the nucleus.

rubric.why: A subshell is a division of a shell.
rubric.description: Defines a subshell as a division of a shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a subshell is a division of a shell.

modelAnswer: A shell is a main energy level around the nucleus in which electrons are present.
A subshell is a division of a shell; subshells are denoted by s, p, d and f.

items.followUp: What is the first ionization energy of an atom? Give its commonly used unit.

rubric.why: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.description: Defines ionization energy, including the gaseous-atom condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the energy needed to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.

rubric.why: A commonly used unit of ionization energy is kilojoule per mole.
rubric.description: Gives a valid unit of ionization energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid unit, such as kJ mol⁻¹ or electron volt.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from the outermost shell of an isolated gaseous atom.
Its commonly used unit is kilojoule per mole (kJ mol⁻¹).

rubric.why: Metallic bonding involves positive metal ions in the metal structure.
rubric.description: Identifies positive metal ions as part of metallic bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying positive metal ions.

rubric.why: A metallic bond is the electrostatic attraction between positive metal ions and delocalized electrons.
rubric.description: Describes the attraction between positive metal ions and delocalized or free electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the electrostatic attraction between positive metal ions and delocalized/free electrons.

modelAnswer: A metallic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between positive metal ions and delocalized (free) electrons.

items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten but not when solid?

rubric.why: Ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points.
rubric.description: Gives one property: high melting points or high boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionic compounds have high melting points or high boiling points.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.description: Gives a second distinct property: electrical conductivity when molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state.

items.followUp: What is meant by the term crystalline solid? Give two examples.

rubric.why: Amorphous solids lack a regular arrangement of particles.
rubric.description: Defines an amorphous solid by the absence of a regular particle arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its particles have no regular arrangement.

rubric.why: Glass and plastic are examples of amorphous solids.
rubric.description: Gives two examples of amorphous solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving both glass and plastic as examples.

modelAnswer: Amorphous solids are solids whose particles have no regular arrangement.
